Hi Ellen — appreciate the note. Short answer: we can accommodate a smoothing mechanism but need to tighten the trigger matrix and define exact computation so it produces predictable outcomes for both sides.

High-level proposal (reasonable starting point):
- Monthly smoothing with a rolling 3-month lookback.
- Corridor: 10% as proposed, but corridor must be applied to normalized monthly usage (see below).
- Retroactive settlement limited to 90 days (calendar) from the end of the affected month; absolute cap on a single settlement event of 25% of that quarter's invoice to avoid large clawbacks.
- Clawback threshold: adjustments only applied when normalized usage deviates by >10% for two consecutive months (prevents single-month noise).

I attached a draft Annex (proposed_rebate_annex_rishi_v1.docx) with redline-style language and a sample formula. Key items we flagged for legal: definition of "normalized usage", audit window, and rounding/units when applying % bands. Also called out billing timing and when credits are applied.

If that direction works, Kimberly can provide legal redlines and Neha can add a sample calc that maps to billing flows. Aim to turn this into a clean Order Form Annex + one-page sample calc that procurement can attach to the SOW.

I’ll stand by for legal notes.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Ellen / Rishi — I reviewed Rishi's draft Annex and MedRx procurement asks. A few redline suggestions from legal:

1) Retroactivity cap and timing
- We can accept a 90-day retroactivity window as requested, but propose an absolute cap on cumulative retroactive adjustments per rolling 12-month period (suggest: 35% of total billed for that 12-month period) to manage tail-risk.

2) Clawback trigger and corridor language
- Replace ambiguous "normalized usage" with: "Adjusted Monthly Usage = billed usage for the month, normalized by the weighted-average baseline over the immediately preceding three full months, excluding months with outages or Force Majeure events."
- Corridor: 10% corridor OK, but tie it to Adjusted Monthly Usage and require two consecutive months beyond corridor to trigger settlement.

3) Audit and records
- Add explicit rights to request supporting usage reports for the 12 months preceding a claim; limit audits to one per 12 months unless material discrepancy (>5%) found.

4) Interest and payment mechanics
- If a credit is owed to the customer, credit will be applied to the next invoice within 45 days of settlement. If Redwood issues an invoice for underbilling, customer will pay within 30 days of settlement. Do not agree to interest other than nominal statutory interest beyond payment terms.

5) Carveouts and exceptions
- Add explicit carveouts for pilot programs, free trials, and known non-production traffic (these should be excluded from all calculations).

I redlined the draft and attached ExhibitB_Redline_KP.docx. Two commercial asks for your consideration, Ellen: (a) remove the absolute cap on single-settlement events would be helpful to Redwood — otherwise large spikes could be unrecoverable; (b) allow Redwood to propose an alternative smoothing window (e.g., 6-month EWMA) if the customer volume pattern is highly seasonal.

If MedRx needs the 90-day limit and 10% corridor as non-negotiable, we can accept but want the cumulative 12-month cap to stay for operational risk reasons.

Happy to hop on a quick call today if helpful.

—Kimberly
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
